title: How often you playtest your own projects?
author: Reckonerxy
selftext:
Hey there! Currently like the rest of you, I'm working on my game and as keep expanding the project and adding new features, I realized that I'm spending more time testing my own game than actually working on it. If I find a bug or I feel the gameplay could be improved, I ask claude to tweak or update the project, so I think this has helped me a lot to keep working on the project, as I try to make the game fun. I also try to also show of the game to more people so I can get even more feedback. So I feel I'm reaching a point that working with AI is not the only step of development.

So I'm wondering, are you also playing you own games as well? or you rather leave it to the AI to debug?

Also FYI here is my project! I have been working for it about 5 months, music/SFX are not implemented yet, but I feel is coming along. Also if you like, you can share you own game as well so I can give you feedback too!

[https://teotlan.com](https://teotlan.com)

comments.author: crypticevincar
comments.body: I playtest my own stuff constantly, note what I find, take screen shot and feed it back into the LLM for adjustment. Getting outside playtesters has never worked for me.

comments.author: No-Mountain-8741
comments.body: run short playtest loops after each small mechanic, not after every feature, and log one fixed seed or input replay so AI debugs the exact run. let AI handle crash logs and repro steps, keep fun calls manual. i made a little arcade game called OrbFrenzy and still do a 3-minute same-seed run after each patch to keep testing from eating the whole day.

comments.author: gamerqc
comments.body:
Both are playable yes. My ARPG already has more than 56,000 lines of code though so it's huge. My other little project has a much more limited/defined scope, so lately I've switched to this one as I kinda see the light at the end of the road, which is not the case with my first game. 

Game 1 (ARPG) has so many features it kinda makes my head hurts when I think about it haha, but it's ambitious and a Phantasy Star Online-inspired game. Not a small task. 

Game 2 (Survival/Action) is inspired by horror movies and games. You defend your cabin against relentless waves of infected, while a Game Director akin to Left 4 Dead adjusts. You set traps, get reward cards after each round. The game's main mode is complete, but I need to test it a lot more. I'm also creating specific challenges, and built it with coop in mind from the get-go (two players max via a game host for now). I have so much fun playing, it's gory and low poly, with absolutely no soundtrack as of now but ambient sounds and effects. 

\*\*\*  
So right now I'd say my focus is on Game 2, whilst Game 1 is a bit on the backburner.
